correctness.rationale: For three colors, encoding edge color differences by signs in Z/3Z makes internal non-CDVs exactly the sign changes. The q+1 constant-sign runs each have per-color CDV counts differing by at most one, yielding a-c<=q+1. Together with n-2=a+b+c+q this proves n>=2a+b+1, while the diagonal total-CDV count gives n>=3r+2. Explicit periodic/gadget color words attain every lower bound. The two-color branch is the unique bipartition coloring, and degree two excludes four or more colors. Exhaustive replay independently stress-tested all proof components on finite ranges.

value.rationale: The initiating paper makes cycles its canonical degree-two exact family. Paths are the other fundamental connected maximum-degree-two family, and the result gives a complete all-sequence classification rather than one numerical instance. The sharp off-diagonal formula N(r,s,t)=2r+s+1 and its independence from t arise from a structural sign-run imbalance lemma, providing a reusable description of how boundary effects change the cycle problem.
